hook: SCP-4002 opens behind an O5-only seal, then turns into something closer to an archaeological dossier: letters from a para-archaeology department, colorized fragments of a Sumerian king list, lines of epic verse, and finally a council meeting. Don't skim the poetry, because the article keeps its actual argument inside those tablet passages. It also pays to track who is writing to whom and in which year, since the letters run from 1907 to 1921 and are addressed to someone called simply the Administrator.
whyItMatters:
Instead of a creature or an object, the thing contained here is an agreement, and the containment procedures are almost entirely about suppressing a story and the evidence behind it. That makes it a concept piece about the Foundation's own premises rather than about a new threat.

It also reaches back into the organization's early years, with an Administrator, a task force that can dress up as insurgents, and names like Project Lazarus and Project Thaumiel attached to the plot. The final meeting asks the Overseers what they would do if their founding assumption turned out to be wrong.
thingsToNotice:
The stele finishes Etana's myth. Refused the Seed by every god he visits, he flies past heaven to the Black Moon, where a king beyond time grants it in return for his people's nature for an age: beasts go quiet, the old gods fade, and when the Black Moon howls the life that was bought will wane and the sacrificed soul come back. The council reads this as humanity itself having once been anomalous, which is why one Overseer asks whether they have been locking up the only normal ones all along.

The letters carry a quieter betrayal. Carter cares about the truth of humanity's past, while Loyd wants the Seed for Lazarus; O5-1 sends Loyd along with leave to kill Carter, but it is Loyd who wounds Carter and runs, only to be killed by Red Right Hand wearing their insurgency disguise. The seed he carried, from an extinct Judean date palm, becomes Anomalous Item-001 and goes to Zartion. The meeting ends by choosing to use it to finish Lazarus, replacing a blighted crop with cuttings of its former self as often as needed.
